entities.label: Jesus’ ministry

scholarly.note: Chronology of the public ministry varies by a few years; region cues matter more than exact dates.

entities.traditionalNote: Public ministry centered in Galilee with journeys to Judea and Jerusalem.
entities.bio: Public ministry centered in Galilee with journeys south to Judea and Jerusalem under Roman rule.

entities.label: Acts

scholarly.note: Narrative ends with Paul in Rome; composition is often placed decades after the earliest events.

entities.traditionalNote: From Jerusalem witness to Paul’s missions across the Roman world.
entities.bio: From Jerusalem witness to Paul’s missions across the Roman world.
kings: Herodian rulers; Roman governors and emperors in the narrative (to early Nero era)

entities.label: James

scholarly.note: Some see very early Jewish-Christian wisdom; others a later circular letter.

entities.traditionalNote: Practical wisdom on faith lived out.
entities.bio: Practical wisdom on faith lived out.

entities.label: Galatians

scholarly.note: Widely accepted as Pauline; exact year depends on North/South Galatia theories.

entities.traditionalNote: Paul’s letter on gospel and covenant to churches in Galatia.
entities.bio: Paul’s letter on the gospel and covenant to congregations in Galatia.

entities.label: 1 Thessalonians

scholarly.note: Among Paul’s earliest surviving letters; strong scholarly consensus on authenticity.

entities.traditionalNote: Early Pauline encouragement to a young Macedonian congregation.
entities.bio: Early encouragement to a young Macedonian congregation.

entities.label: 2 Thessalonians

scholarly.note: Some accept Pauline authorship soon after 1 Thessalonians; others argue for a later hand.

entities.traditionalNote: Follow-up on endurance and the day of the Lord.
entities.bio: Follow-up on endurance and the day of the Lord.
kings: Early Pauline period or later, depending on view

entities.label: 1 Corinthians

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; written from Ephesus to a fractious Corinthian church.

entities.traditionalNote: Pastoral letter addressing division, worship, and resurrection hope.
entities.bio: Addresses division, worship, and resurrection hope in a fractious port city church.

entities.label: 2 Corinthians

scholarly.note: Pauline; some see it as combining more than one letter fragment.

region.origin: Paul on the move in Macedonia/Asia

entities.traditionalNote: Paul defends his apostleship and reconciles with Corinth.
entities.bio: Paul defends his apostleship and seeks reconciliation with Corinth.

entities.label: Romans

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; usually placed near the end of the Aegean mission period.

entities.traditionalNote: Paul’s sustained presentation of the gospel to the Roman churches.
entities.bio: Sustained presentation of the gospel to the Roman churches before Paul’s journey there.

entities.label: Philippians

scholarly.note: Accepted as Pauline; scholars debate whether from Rome, Ephesus, or Caesarea.

entities.traditionalNote: Joyful letter from custody to a supportive Macedonian church.
entities.bio: Joyful letter from imprisonment to a supportive Macedonian church.
kings: Nero (if Roman custody) or mid-50s provincial custody

entities.label: Philemon

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; closely tied to the Onesimus situation and often to Colossians.

entities.traditionalNote: Personal appeal concerning Onesimus.
entities.bio: Personal appeal concerning Onesimus.

entities.label: Colossians

scholarly.note: Some attribute to Paul in custody; others see a later Pauline school.

entities.traditionalNote: Christ-centered letter to a church Paul may not have visited.
entities.bio: Christ-centered letter to a church Paul may not have visited.

entities.label: Ephesians

scholarly.note: Many scholars see a circular Pauline-tradition letter rather than a situation-specific note from Paul.

entities.traditionalNote: Broad teaching on church unity and life in Christ.
entities.bio: Broad teaching on church unity and life in Christ.

entities.label: Pastoral Epistles

scholarly.note: 1–2 Timothy and Titus are frequently dated after Paul’s death as church-order letters in his name.

entities.traditionalNote: 1–2 Timothy and Titus on leadership and sound teaching.
entities.bio: 1–2 Timothy and Titus on leadership and sound teaching.
kings: Late Nero or later 1st-century setting (views differ)

entities.label: 1 Peter

scholarly.note: Traditional Petrine authorship is debated; addresses believers under social pressure in Asia Minor.

entities.traditionalNote: Hope and holiness for Christians facing hostility.
entities.bio: Hope and holiness for Christians facing social hostility.

entities.label: Hebrews

scholarly.dateLabel: Author unknown; often pre- or post-70
scholarly.note: Not Pauline in most modern critical views; a sophisticated sermon on Christ’s priesthood.

entities.traditionalNote: Anonymous sermon-letter exalting Christ over earlier covenants.
entities.bio: Anonymous sermon-letter exalting Christ’s priesthood over earlier covenants.

entities.label: Mark

scholarly.note: Most scholars treat Mark as the earliest Gospel, written around the Jewish War / temple crisis.

region.setting: Roman world (audience often linked with Rome)

entities.traditionalNote: Action-focused Gospel traditionally linked with Peter’s preaching.
entities.bio: The shortest Gospel, centered on Jesus’ ministry, cross, and empty tomb; often read as the earliest narrative template.
kings: Nero to early Vespasian era (composition window)

entities.label: Destruction of the temple

scholarly.note: Fixed Roman-Jewish War anchor; often used when dating Mark and the Synoptics relative to the temple’s fall.

entities.traditionalNote: Rome destroys the Jerusalem temple under Titus during the Jewish War.
entities.bio: A watershed for Judaism and for reading the Gospels—especially passages about the temple and Jerusalem’s crisis.
kings: Vespasian / Titus (Rome); end of the Second Temple

entities.label: Matthew

scholarly.note: Usually dated after Mark, with strong Jewish-Christian teaching for a synagogue-aware audience.

region.setting: Likely Syrian / Jewish-Christian setting (e.g. Antioch area)

entities.traditionalNote: Gospel presenting Jesus as Messiah and teacher of the kingdom, attributed to Matthew.
entities.bio: Structured teaching Gospel with sermons and fulfillment themes, bridging Jewish Scripture and the church’s mission.
kings: Flavian period if later dating; earlier if traditional

entities.label: Luke

scholarly.note: Usually paired with Acts and placed after Mark; emphasizes ordered narrative for a broader audience.

entities.traditionalNote: Careful narrative Gospel traditionally from Luke, companion of Paul.
entities.bio: Ordered account of Jesus’ life with attention to the Spirit, the poor, and the path to Jerusalem.
kings: Flavian period if later dating; earlier if traditional

entities.label: 1 John

scholarly.note: Usually linked to Johannine circles in Asia Minor rather than a simple private note from the apostle.

entities.traditionalNote: Tests of discipleship: truth, love, and confession of Christ.
entities.bio: Tests of discipleship: truth, love, and confession of Christ.

entities.label: John

scholarly.note: Often placed last among the four; many see a Johannine community shaping a distinctive theological witness.

entities.traditionalNote: Theological Gospel attributed to John, emphasizing Jesus’ identity and signs.
entities.bio: Distinctive Gospel of signs, long discourses, and high Christology culminating in the cross and resurrection.

entities.label: Revelation

scholarly.note: Apocalypse to Asian churches; majority prefer a late-1st-century Roman setting.

region.setting: Patmos and the seven churches of Asia

entities.traditionalNote: Visions of judgment and hope under imperial pressure.
entities.bio: Visions of judgment and hope under imperial pressure.
